agent_blocked_on.what_I_did: I did NOT apply the rule off the broken flag. I left the scanned `lowercase_in_target` untouched for audit, and added `lowercase_in_target_recomputed` per member: a CASE-SENSITIVE search of the raw target for the all-lowercase form of the token, which is the signal the rule actually wants (does this wrong-form also occur as an ordinary lowercase word, such that a re.IGNORECASE replacement would corrupt prose). Exactly one actionable member has the recomputed flag set: cluster 32 'Talus' -> Talos, because line 733 reads 'the stylized, jagged lightning bolt of talus' in lowercase. That lowercase occurrence is itself the god mis-cased, not the anatomical noun, so an IGNORECASE rule fixes both rather than corrupting prose — but the orchestrator should still run the corpus-wide check on 'talus' before writing the row. Every other confirm / different_canonical / new_canon member is clean under the recomputed gate.
